generation.ceiling_is: UPPER BOUND -- assumes the launches pipeline perfectly with zero per-example process overhead, which they will not. It answers 'could generation ever feed this model', not 'what will it actually reach'.

correction_to_6_7.why: 6.7 divided sum(invocation_medians_ms) -- TWO medians per row -- by total_launches -- FORTY per row (20 trials x 2 invocations). That understates the per-launch kernel by exactly n_invocations = 2, i.e. 20x.
correction_to_6_7.consequence: overhead fraction is 99.970%, not 99.998%. The CONCLUSION is unchanged -- overhead still dominates by three orders of magnitude -- but the ceiling derived from the corrected figure (7,911 ex/s) is the number that decides which model sizes can ever be fed, and the wrong one would have understated it.

decision.bottleneck: DATA GENERATION, at every model size measured
decision.why: Generation produces 2.39 ex/s today. Training consumes 233-14,583 ex/s. So training is never the constraint, and no training-side optimisation can change that: the constraint is how fast examples are produced.
decision.and_the_non_obvious_part: Removing the per-example process overhead -- the obvious fix, and the one 6.7 identified -- raises generation to at most 7,911 ex/s. That unblocks medium and large, but STILL DOES NOT feed small. The residual constraint is the MEASUREMENT PROTOCOL: 40 launches per example at 3.16 us each is 126 us of GPU work per example, so halving the trial count would double the ceiling. That is a protocol decision about statistical rigour, not a GPU or a training problem.
what_would_actually_help: batch or persist the measurement worker: worth ~3,312x
reduce launches per example (currently 40), which raises the ceiling proportionally -- but it trades against the trial count 6.6.1 justified, so it is a statistical decision, not a free win
NOT training optimisation, and NOT a faster GPU

caveats: Throughput, not end-to-end wall clock for a whole run. The two sides were measured in separate jobs on a shared GPU.

The training side consumed SYNTHETIC batches (torch.randint), not real dataset rows, because the model cannot accept the real feature width yet (gpu-sim-u2o.12.1 finding 3). Its rate is a property of the model and batch shape, not of the data.
The overhead-free ceiling is an UPPER bound assuming perfect pipelining; real batching will land below it.
'The v1 model size' is undefined, so a ladder was profiled (gpu-sim-u2o.12.1). A decision about 'the v1 model' is therefore a decision about a ladder, and should be restated once a size is chosen.
